html:
Sirmium was a Roman city on the Sava River, today's Sremska Mitrovica in northern Serbia, which became one of the four capitals of the empire under Diocletian's tetrarchy in 294.

The Danube frontier was the empire's main front, and the region gave Rome many soldier emperors; more than a dozen were born in today's Serbia, among them Constantine the Great, born at Naissus, now Niš. Sirmium had an imperial palace, a hippodrome and a mint, and church councils met there in the 300s. The city was sacked by the Huns in 441 and fell to the Avars in 582 after a long siege. Its ruins lie under the modern town in Serbia.
sum: Sirmium was a Roman city on the Sava River, today's Sremska Mitrovica in northern Serbia, which became one of the four capitals of the empire under Diocletian's tetrarchy in 294.
